title: Featured: codeSplitter
intro: The code host for the agentic era. Much of the other work exists because of it. [Try it](https://codesplitter.notryanquinn.workers.dev).

apps.name: codeSplitter
apps.line: A code host for the agentic era. Each file is a Durable Object, and agents edit line by line. It has real git on Cloudflare Artifacts and an MCP server. One codebase runs on the edge and as a desktop app. [Try it](https://codesplitter.notryanquinn.workers.dev)

title: Games
intro: These are for fun. Most of them play in the browser, and each one runs as a desktop app. They are in the same order as in eqosys.

apps.name: Park Hide & Seek
apps.line: 3D hide and seek on real Yosemite terrain. The page, a LAN host or the edge can run the game. Each player gets only what they can see. [Play it](https://park-hide-seek.notryanquinn.workers.dev)

apps.name: Git Recon
apps.line: A repo as a shooter level. Its folders become compounds and its files become buildings, on real ground (Yosemite, or any lat/long) or in a plastic-army kitchen and garden. Git commands are the weapons. Play alone in the page, with up to 64 players in a LAN battle, or online in a Durable Object for each room.

apps.name: Skate Tech Park
apps.line: Skate a street spot, or fly a rocket roadster with ten cold-gas thrusters across the gap. It is a three.js page on a pure fixed-step sim, which the tests run headless.

apps.name: Alien Disc Golf
apps.line: Disc golf where the course is the planet: nine holes between random countries on a three.js globe. NOAA's live wind carries the disc, and a high throw rides the jet stream. The Worker relays the latest GFS grid from NOMADS, and the page decodes the GRIB2. Guess the tee's country to get one stroke back.

apps.name: Delayed Reaction
apps.line: A phone-first rhythm game. You sprint through a neon tunnel that rolls. A ring calls a note, and you answer one bar later on one of four thumb pads. Your answers echo back through a dub delay. The sim plays in beats with no page, and thus a test runs each level.

apps.name: Two Fronts
apps.line: Thunder Marines against the Wooka horde: a turn-based galactic war with three.js hero battles in orbit and on six worlds. There is one world for each kind of sector: redwood forest, desert, ruined city, glowing alien night, beach and deep-space station. The two parts were built apart and connect through small JSON types (a spec in, a result out). Play the AI or hotseat in the page, or a friend online through a Durable Object for each campaign.

apps.name: Hippo Tycoon
apps.line: One game class runs as a Durable Object on Cloudflare and in-process in the binary: solo, couch, LAN party and online rooms.

apps.name: Super Spy Splat Shot
apps.line: A spy game in a pitch-dark Gaussian-splat room. A short config makes the three.js page a desktop app, and the same page races friends online on a Worker.

apps.name: Mythic Masters
apps.line: A 3D creature arena brawler where mass, height and stats shape each body, and flyers must come down. A headless bot-vs-bot tuner keeps 76 folklore beasts near a 50% win rate, from a 6 kg jackalope to a one-tonne lake monster. One arena layout has a skin for each built region, on a route of 64.

apps.name: Excalibrawl
apps.line: A drawing fight each hour. Clef and Clef Flash select only a move, shape, colour, grid cell and size from a picture of their halves. Or two text models write a drawing language that uses few tokens. Clef is the referee, and a fight costs two cents or less. Replays are in R2, and a Durable Object has the live socket.

title: One account, one front door
intro: These connect the apps: one sign-in for all of them, and one page that lists them.

apps.name: eqosys
apps.line: Your home for each Q game: your games, friends, saves and studio on one account. Below it is Better Auth on D1, with a PKCE code handoff to each app and a signed token that the app can check alone. It knows which app each person came from and what they can do in each. A Durable Object for each person holds friends, presence and notifications. It is also a plain OpenID provider for a site's own Better Auth or a native app. PolyForm Noncommercial.

apps.name: Playground
apps.line: One page that lists each app with a way to try it: Play, Download or Source. It has static assets only, and thus it costs nothing.

apps.name: Qollab
apps.line: Realtime rooms for any app on Cloudflare: rooms, seats, parties, presence and saves in one call. It is built into eqosys as its own Worker, with a Durable Object for each player and each room. PolyForm Noncommercial.

title: My apps
intro: Real tools for real work. Some have their own license.

apps.name: What Would Fantano Say
apps.line: A parody music critic as an RWSDK Worker. The phone decodes the song and selects a 15 s clip. Cloudflare's Clef-omni judges it for approximately $5 for each 100,000 reviews. It is behind a rate limit, Turnstile, an edge cache and a daily budget.

apps.name: One Team in 32
apps.line: One static page ("One Team in 32"), which a Cloudflare Worker serves as plain assets. There is no Worker code.

apps.name: qCRM
apps.line: A CRM with MCP built in, a Rust wasm engine in the browser, office sync, signed webhooks and a desktop build. It has roles for a real place and hashed org ids. PolyForm Noncommercial.

apps.name: GeoBoxQ
apps.line: A fit checker for shipping boxes, with a Rust engine that packs boxes in boxes. PolyForm Noncommercial.

apps.name: AT Lens
apps.line: Type a handle and watch the AT Protocol work: domain to DID to data server to typed records, checked in the two directions. Then see the account live on the Jetstream firehose. Sign in with atproto OAuth to write a record of our own Lexicon and watch it come back. No keys and no bindings.

apps.name: ShareSplat
apps.line: Product photos become a 3D spin for a store page. A guided shot list on the phone takes six sides for an AI-guessed mesh, or 72 photos in rings for a real Gaussian splat. A turntable splat viewer has a Shopify embed that you paste in.

apps.name: GeoBoxQ for Shopify
apps.line: A small wrapper that turns a Shopify cart into the store's own box.

apps.name: QView3D
apps.line: A 3D product customiser for a shop page, from one script tag. Shoppers drag a photo over a hat or onto a tee or hoodie's front, back and sleeve, choose its colour and save a snapshot. A shop with another product makes a model of it from photos. Uploads go to R2 on signed links, in one folder for each org. PolyForm Noncommercial.

apps.name: artstewengine
apps.line: A small RWSDK app on D1 with a Better Auth admin page. Add who has paid, and the sealed engine of qCRM gets its key only for a paid license.

title: The workshop
intro: Music, 3D and circuits: tools to make things. Where it helps, a Rust engine runs with a TypeScript engine.

apps.name: Splat Rooms
apps.line: A splat hunt game with a world class. Its 30 MB scenes stream from a folder on your disk and are never embedded.

apps.name: FM Groovebox
apps.line: One Rust crate runs as wasm in the audio thread and through FFI on the host. Its output is bit-identical to the TypeScript engine.

apps.name: Motion MIDI
apps.line: One synth in Rust and in TypeScript, checked sample by sample

apps.name: Auto Rig
apps.line: Auto-rigging a 3D model in Rust and TypeScript with identical output

apps.name: Meshy Studio
apps.line: A folder-based batch tool for the Meshy API: image, multi-image and text to 3D, texture, remesh, rig, animate and concept art. Your key stays local, and you see the price before each spend.

apps.name: Splat Desktop
apps.line: PlayCanvas' SuperSplat editor as a desktop app. It works on a folder on your disk.

apps.name: tscircuit Desktop
apps.line: A heavy, real-world Vite app as one file, with a Rust engine up to 22x faster and a TypeScript fallback

apps.name: Pixel RAG
apps.line: Add your screenshots and find the parts that look the same in all of them. Each worker, web or desktop, shares one Rust index.

title: Everything else: frameworks, other people's apps and test fixtures
intro: Sample apps from frameworks and apps from other people, which run with no code changes. Also the small apps that the tests use. A new app goes here first, until someone moves it to its section.

apps.name: Hello World
apps.line: The first five minutes: a twenty-line page. The welcome tour finds it, lets three agents write it again at the same time, and then asks you to deploy it.

apps.name: Kitesurf Bench
apps.line: Times Cloudflare's Kitesurf agent browser against Chromium on our own live pages, from inside a Worker. Deploy, press Run, copy the table, destroy.

apps.name: Agent Office
apps.line: Someone else's Node server (PTYs, WebSockets, a 3D client) as one binary, nothing forked

apps.name: TerraViz
apps.line: TerraViz is the Science On a Sphere globe of The Zyra Project (Apache-2.0, not ours). We clone it and run it with no code changes. Shared Sphere adds a room on one globe and a teacher's lock, so that a class follows one pair of hands. NOAA tour scripts stay in step on each screen, and a small Rust crate reads them as slides.

apps.name: Nuxt
apps.line: A Nuxt 4 app on the `cloudflare-module` preset of Nitro (one KV binding), as a desktop app with no edits. `init` reads it, and the host runs the Worker that Nitro built. The same shared HTTP journey checks it.

apps.name: Qwik City
apps.line: A Qwik City app on its own `cloudflare-pages` adapter, as a desktop app with no edits. A `routeLoader$` and a `routeAction$` count in KV through `platform.env`. `init` reads the adapter's `dist/_worker.js` as it is.

apps.name: Astro
apps.line: An Astro site on `@astrojs/cloudflare`, as a desktop app with no edits. A server page and an API route count in KV through `cloudflare:workers`. `init` reads it as it is.

apps.name: Elysia
apps.line: An Elysia Worker as the Cloudflare guide of Elysia writes it (`aot: false`, `cloudflare:workers`), as a desktop app with no edits. `init` now reads Elysia.

apps.name: SvelteKit
apps.line: A SvelteKit 3 app on the Cloudflare adapter, as a desktop app with no edits. It has a `load` from KV and a form action that increments it. It meets the same sample app contract as hono-example, and the same shared journey checks it.

apps.name: SolidStart
apps.line: A SolidStart 2 app on the `cloudflare_module` preset of Nitro, as a desktop app with no edits. A `"use server"` query and an API route count in KV through `cloudflare:workers`. `rustybuns init` reads it as it is.

apps.name: React Router
apps.line: React Router 7 on Cloudflare's own template (`workers/app.ts`, the Vite plugin, a loader and an action on KV), as a desktop app with no edits. It is the second framework on the shared sample-app journey.

apps.name: Next.js
apps.line: A Next.js 16 app on `@opennextjs/cloudflare` (one KV binding), as a desktop app with no edits. `init` reads it, and the host runs the `worker.js` that OpenNext built. The same shared HTTP journey checks it.

apps.name: Svelte SPA
apps.line: A client-only Svelte 5 + Vite app (no server) as a desktop app. Its counter is in a `"use server"` action that the host runs.

apps.name: Vue SPA
apps.line: A client-only Vue 3 + Vite app (no server) as a desktop app. Its counter is in a `"use server"` action that the host runs.

apps.name: Solid SPA
apps.line: A client-only Solid + Vite app (no server) as a desktop app. Its counter is in a `"use server"` action that the host runs.

apps.name: Hono
apps.line: A Hono Worker from Hono's own docs (one KV binding), as a desktop app with no edits. It is the sample app contract that each framework example meets, and one shared HTTP journey checks it.

apps.name: Elysia RealWorld
apps.line: The RealWorld backend of bedstack (Elysia, Drizzle, postgres.js) with no source edits. It is a desktop binary on PGlite that passes their Postman suite. The doc lists the five ways that it breaks on Workers.

apps.name: TanStack Start
apps.line: TanStack Start on Cloudflare's Vite plugin (server functions, a server route, D1 and KV) as a desktop app with no code changes.

apps.name: Agent Demo
apps.line: A small snack-vote Worker that is seeded into codeSplitter. Some coding agents can build it at the same time and resolve a merge conflict on camera.

apps.name: Borg Postgres
apps.line: A Postgres app keeps its database and moves its code: Hyperdrive on the edge, PGlite on the desktop.

apps.name: Borg
apps.line: Not an app: a small Worker that uses each binding one time. Thus one suite can check the local twins against a real deploy.

apps.name: SPA fixture
apps.line: Not an app: a part of a real RWSDK game. The tests use it to check that `init` reads it correctly.

apps.name: Worker example
apps.line: A full Worker (D1, KV, a Durable Object) as a desktop binary in half a second, and a Rust FFI probe with a TypeScript fallback.
